components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is
            assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits.
            The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+' (e.g. '0412 345 678'
            is stored as '+61412345678'); the stored and returned value is that
            E.164 string.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. When omitted on create it
            defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'
            format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only hint used only when creating an owner. When true, an owner
            may be created even though another owner already has the same last name
            and address (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace);
            otherwise such a request is rejected with 409 Conflict. This flag is
            never persisted or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone

      title: Owner

        - type: object
          properties:

              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true

              description: >-

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` feature. The codebase already had partial support (a `sharesHousehold` write-only flag that skipped the 409 household-duplicate check); I completed it so it fully satisfies the spec and assigns a stable shared `householdId`.

Changes:

1. **`Owner` model** (`model/Owner.java`) — added a persisted `householdId` field (`household_id` column) with getter/setter.

2. **Schema DDL** — added a `household_id` column to the `owners` table in all four schema files (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `mysql`, `postgres`), since the test profile uses `ddl-auto=none` and loads `schema.sql`.

4. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — restructured the household logic:
   - Collect existing owners in the same household (same normalized last name + address).
   - If a match exists and `sharesHousehold` is not true → `409 Conflict` (unchanged behavior).
   - If a match exists and `sharesHousehold` is true → allow creation, compute a deterministic `householdId` and assign it to the new owner **and** every existing household member (persisting them), so all members share the same value.
   - Added a `householdId(...)` helper deriving a stable identifier as the upper-cased first 12 hex chars of `SHA-256("<lastNameKey>|<addressKey>")` — deterministic, so every joiner gets an identical, non-blank id.

5. **Mapper** — no change needed; MapStruct auto-maps `householdId` between `Owner` and `OwnerDto`.

The two feature tests (`OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.createOwnerHouseholdDuplicateAllowedWhenSharesHousehold` and `AcceptanceTest.coreJoinersShareHouseholdId`) pass, as does the entire suite (257 tests, 0 failures).

   - Collect existing owners in the same household (same normalized last name + address).
   - If a match exists and `sharesHousehold` is not true → `409 Conflict` (unchanged behavior).
   - If a match exists and `sharesHousehold` is true → allow creation, compute a deterministic `householdId` and assign it to the new owner **and** every existing household member (persisting them), so all members share the same value.
   - Added a `householdId(...)` helper deriving a stable identifier as the upper-cased first 12 hex chars of `SHA-256("<lastNameKey>|<addressKey>")` — deterministic, so every joiner gets an identical, non-blank id.

5. **Mapper** — no change needed; MapStruct auto-maps `householdId` between `Owner` and `OwnerDto`.
